title: Counting rat tails (derived carousel, carries Fri 13 Nov mind.the.gap, piece f3fcd5e1)

five_whys.q: Why did Meta and Amazon staff burn AI on nothing?
five_whys.a: They were ranked on leaderboards by how many tokens, the units of AI use, they ran up.

five_whys.q: Why were they ranked by use?
five_whys.a: Bosses made AI use part of reviews, and use is the cheapest thing to measure.

five_whys.q: Why does ranking by use go wrong?
five_whys.a: Pay people for a sign of what you want and they make signs: Hanoi paid per rat tail in 1902 and got rat farms.

five_whys.q: Why is this bigger than two companies?
five_whys.a: A study of a 5,000-person firm found halving its AI-use target cut junk queries and lifted sales 7%, and Meta, Amazon and Duolingo have backed down.

five_whys.q: Why should an everyday business person care?
five_whys.a: A usage number is the AI bill, not the result; judge people on it and they run up the bill, so judge AI on a number you already track.

explains.tokens: the bits of text an AI reads and writes, each one billed (cover line)
explains.token: the bits of text an AI reads and writes, each one billed (cover line)

cards.headline: Meta staff were ranked by AI use. They gamed it
cards.line: AI use is counted in tokens, the bits of text an AI reads and writes. Each costs money.
cards.picture: Cover scene: a podium trophy reading TOKEN LEGEND, a pile of cut rat tails on the top step

cards.headline: Staff ran pointless AI jobs to climb.
cards.line: Meta's board tracked the tokens of 85,000 staff. Amazon staff set AI helpers on needless tasks.
cards.picture: A leaderboard, top row TOKEN LEGEND, the token count meter spinning past 60 trillion

cards.headline: Pay for a number, and people fake it.
cards.line: In 1902 Hanoi paid a cent per rat tail. People cut tails off and farmed rats.
cards.picture: A live rat with no tail beside a stack of tails and a one-cent coin

cards.headline: Asking for less AI use lifted sales 7%.
cards.line: One firm asked 5,000 staff for half the AI queries. Nine in ten dropped were junk.
cards.picture: Two bars: queries down about 30%, sales up 7%, junk queries struck through
cards.source: arXiv preprint, Sep 2026, a medical-device firm's AI query target cut from 200 to 100 a month (not yet peer reviewed)

cards.headline: Three big firms dropped AI-use scores.
cards.line: Meta, Amazon and Duolingo. Amazon: no AI help is 'a finding, not a failing.'
cards.picture: Three U-turn arrows, one each for Meta, Amazon and Duolingo
cards.source: daily.dev (Meta, Sep 2026); CNBC (Amazon memo, Oct 2026); WPXI (Duolingo, Apr 2026)

cards.headline: Stop scoring AI use.
cards.line: Take it out of review forms, dashboards and team charts.
cards.picture: A review form with the AI USAGE line crossed out

cards.headline: Judge AI on results, not use.
cards.line: Sales, tickets closed, invoices sent. If it hasn't moved, the AI isn't working yet. Follow for more.
cards.picture: One gauge labelled SALES with its needle, Follow for more over the centred wordmark

read_back.reader: Fresh reader A (Haiku, a small-business owner, headlines only, once; round 2)

answers.what: Meta ranked staff by how much they used AI, and staff gamed the ranking.
answers.happened: Employees ran pointless AI jobs to climb the leaderboard, and three big firms then dropped AI-use scores.
answers.why: When you pay people for a number, they fake the number instead of doing useful work.
answers.so_what: If I score my team by AI use, I will get busywork and no real gain.
answers.do: Judge AI by the results it produces, such as sales and quality, not how often it is used.

read_back.reader: Fresh reader B (Sonnet, a 15-year-old, headlines only, once; round 2)

answers.what: Companies judging workers by how much they use AI, and it backfiring.
answers.happened: Meta ranked staff on AI use, so people ran pointless AI jobs just to look good.
answers.why: When you get ranked on a number, people fake the number instead of doing real work.
answers.so_what: Like being graded on hours studied: I would leave the tab open and learn nothing.
answers.do: Judge AI by the results it gets, not by how much people use it.

read_back_fixed: Round 1 stumbled on 'count a sign' (vague), 'backed down' (from what) and 'a number you track' (seemed to contradict card 6); cards 3, 5 and 7 now say pay for a number, dropped AI-use scores, and judge on results. Round 2 stumbled on 'halving the AI target'; card 4 now says asking for less AI use lifted sales.
